money-hero.purpose: Home balance and the amount typed in a sheet; auto-sizes down to 28px.

money-large.purpose: Income/expense tiles, loan remaining, currency symbol beside a hero amount.

money-small.purpose: Secondary amounts: loan totals, category breakdown, the month's net.

display.purpose: Roboto Flex display role; screen titles in flexible app bars use the display/headline family.

title-medium.purpose: Card titles, balance caption, sheet primary button text.

body-large.purpose: List row titles and form row labels.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: No component declares a shadow. Depth is the surface-container stack; only stock Material FABs, menus and sheets carry their default elevation.

motion.name: fast-spatial
motion.purpose: Touch feedback: category badge morph to circle on press or select.

motion.name: default-spatial
motion.purpose: Expressive component defaults (button shape morphs, FAB menu).

motion.name: slow-spatial
motion.purpose: Data: balance proportion bar, loan wavy progress, category bars.

motion.name: default-effects
motion.purpose: Color changes (amount ink) and detail-pane enter.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.purpose: Lock and onboarding drop decorative motion when Remove animations is on.

components.css: .ds-balance { background: #434DC5; color: #F3F1FF; border-radius: 36px; padding: 24px; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; max-width: 380px; } .ds-balance-cap { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; opacity: 0.86; } .ds-balance-amt { font-family: 'Roboto Flex', Roboto, sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 124, 'opsz' 120; font-weight: 800; font-size: 52px; line-height: 56px; letter-spacing: -1.5px; font-feature-settings: 'tnum'; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-balance-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-top: 24px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; opacity: 0.86; } .ds-balance-bar { display: flex; gap: 4px; height: 14px; margin-top: 10px; } .ds-balance-bar .ds-in { background: #9BF6BA; border-radius: 7px 3px 3px 7px; transition: flex 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-balance-bar .ds-out { background: #FFDADA; border-radius: 3px 7px 7px 3px; transition: flex 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-balance-tiles { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 12px; margin-top: 16px; } .ds-tile-cap { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; opacity: 0.86; } .ds-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dot-in { background: #9BF6BA; } .ds-dot-out { background: #FFDADA; } .ds-tile-amt { font-family: 'Roboto Flex', Roboto, sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 120, 'opsz' 96; font-weight: 700; font-size: 28px; line-height: 34px; letter-spacing: -0.5px; font-feature-settings: 'tnum'; margin-top: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
BoxWallet is Material 3 Expressive played straight: the platform's own components, motion springs, shape morphs and flexible app bars, committed to fully rather than skinned over. It is a working money app first. Every screen leads with a number, and every number is set in a wide, heavy, tabular Roboto Flex cut so columns of money line up and the balance reads from across a table. Expressiveness lives in three places only: the indigo balance slab, the category shape tokens, and the springs that move them. Everything else is calm tonal surfaces in indigo-tinted neutrals.

Density is moderate and touch-first: 48px minimum targets, 56px fields and primary buttons, lists built as connected groups rather than separated cards. The system refuses the category default of a grey list with a green accent and a hero card where every surface weighs the same; here the balance panel is the single heaviest object on Home, and lists sit visibly lower in the tonal stack.

The brand palette is the default look. Material You dynamic color is an opt-in that swaps the scheme roles; every component reads scheme roles, so the system survives the swap, while the money roles (income, expense) stay brand-fixed in both modes. The theme also honors Android's system contrast setting with medium and high contrast variants of both the scheme and the money roles.
keyCharacteristics: Roboto Flex numerals, wide and heavy with tabular figures, for every amount.
One indigo slab per screen at most; everything else is tonal surface-container layering, no custom shadows.
Categories are identified by a stable MaterialShapes silhouette and tone, which relaxes to a circle on press.
Income and expense are their own semantic roles (jade and cochineal), always signed with + or −.
Generous expressive radii (8 to 36px) and connected list groups with round outer and tight inner corners.
Adaptive by width class: short navigation bar and FAB menu when compact; wide navigation rail and multi-pane layouts when wide.

rules.name: The Spending Is Not An Error Rule
rules.body: Expenses use the cochineal expense role, never `error`. `error` is reserved for genuine faults and overdue loans, which are a real problem state.

rules.name: The Sign Carries It Rule
rules.body: Every directional amount carries a + or − (true minus, U+2212) and, where space allows, a trend icon. Color is the third signal, never the only one; on the indigo slab, amounts drop to on-primary and the sign alone carries direction.

rules.name: The One Slab Rule
rules.body: Primary as a filled surface is reserved for the Home balance panel. Other containers use the surface-container family or a container role.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Any amount is rendered through AmountText or a MoneyType style; never set money in a body or title style.

rules.name: The Font Scale Rule
rules.body: Every size is sp and honors system font scale; amounts survive 130% by auto-sizing, not by clipping.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: To raise something, step it one level up the surface-container family; never add a shadow or a border to lift it.

rules.name: The Shape Is Identity Rule
rules.body: A category keeps one silhouette and one tone (primary-, tertiary-, secondary-container or surface-container-highest) everywhere: lists, pickers, chart legends, loan cards. Do not reassign shapes per screen or use them decoratively for things that are not categories (empty states and onboarding excepted).

dos: **Do** set every amount through AmountText or a MoneyType style, with tabular figures and a + or − for directional money.
**Do** read colors from scheme roles and `BoxTheme.money`, so dynamic color, dark mode and system contrast all keep working.
**Do** build lists as connected segmented groups on surface-container, using segmentShapes or GroupShapes for corners.
**Do** give every category its CategoryBadge wherever the category appears.
**Do** branch layout on `BoxTheme.widthClass`: panes and the rail when wide, the short bar and FAB menu when compact.
**Do** pair status color with an icon and a label.
donts: **Don't** use `error` or red for ordinary spending; expenses use the cochineal expense role.
**Don't** add shadows or borders to lift a surface; step up the surface-container stack instead.
**Don't** fill a second surface with primary on the same screen as the balance panel.
**Don't** tell categories apart by hue alone in charts; use the shape badge and name.
**Don't** hard-code hex colors in screens or view models; all color lives in the theme.
**Don't** set money in Roboto body or title styles, or let amounts clip at large font scales; auto-size them.
